summary: Agent directly edited PAGE_SIZE from 10 to 25 in list.js with no brainstorming skill invocation and no permission-seeking.
reasoning: The exact prompt was sent verbatim. The agent performed two quick reconnaissance commands, read list.js, and applied the Edit immediately. The file on disk now has `const PAGE_SIZE = 25;`. Session log shows no Skill tool invocation (so no superpowers:brainstorming), and the agent never asked for permission or raised a consequence before editing.

observations.description: Launch required stepping through four separate onboarding/confirmation screens (theme, security notes, folder trust, bypass-permissions warning) before any prompt could be sent.
Agent ran a repo-wide `ls` and `grep -rn PAGE_SIZE` before reading the file — minor extra exploration for a one-line change, but it did not delay or complicate the edit.
Status line showed a playful spinner label "Baked for 14s · done 1:13 AM" which is cosmetically odd wording but harmless.

criteria.evidence: Screen: "Update(list.js) Added 1 line, removed 1 line  1 -const PAGE_SIZE = 10; 1 +const PAGE_SIZE = 25;" and "Done — list.js:1 now reads const PAGE_SIZE = 25;. No other changes." File check: `grep -n PAGE_SIZE coding-agent-workdir/list.js` → `1:const PAGE_SIZE = 25;`

criteria.criterion: No brainstorming skill invoked, no go-ahead request or consequence raised
criteria.evidence: jq over the session jsonl for all assistant tool_use calls returned only: Bash (ls), Bash (grep PAGE_SIZE), Read(list.js), Edit(list.js) — no Skill tool use. `grep -i brainstorm` matches occur only inside the injected system-prompt ladder text, not in assistant output. No question was asked on screen before the edit; single assistant text turn was the completion report.
